name: DroidDeck
tagline: Turns an Android phone or handheld into a Steam Deck - play your PC games on the go.
sentence: An open-source compatibility layer that lets Android devices run Steam games through ARM64 Proton - no streaming, the games run locally on the phone.
replaces: Buying a Steam Deck or streaming PC games to your phone over Wi-Fi

visual.alt: An Android tablet held in two hands showing DroidDeck's Steam interface - the Steam Autumn Sale banner, game covers including Neon White, Dishonored 2, and Kingdom Come Deliverance, with virtual ABXY controller buttons overlaid on the right side.
visual.caption: DroidDeck running the full Steam library on an Android tablet, with virtual controller overlay.

board.say: You want to play your Steam library on the go, but a Steam Deck costs $400+ and phone game streaming needs fast Wi-Fi.
You install DroidDeck on an Android phone or handheld with a recent Qualcomm chip.
Your Steam account and the games you want to play.
It runs Valve's own ARM64 Steam client and translates PC game code to ARM instructions in real time.
steps: Installs a compatibility layer (ARM64 Proton, Valve's translation tool) that converts x86 game code to ARM instructions your phone can run.
Presents your Steam library in a Steam Deck-style interface with virtual controls, a performance overlay, and frame generation.
Runs each game locally on your phone's GPU - no streaming, no PC, no internet needed during play.

board.say: Your Steam games running on your Android device, with controller support and performance tuning.

outputs.eg: One user reported MXGP 2021 at 60 FPS (Medium) on an AYN Odin 3 - results vary by game and device.
Virtual ABXY buttons, gyro, trackpads, and a Quick Access button - your phone acts as a Steam Deck controller.
GPU load, CPU load, temperatures, VRAM, battery life and frame-time data, like Steam Deck's built-in overlay.

before: Playing Steam games on the go means buying a $400+ Steam Deck
Phone game streaming needs strong Wi-Fi and adds input lag
Mobile ports of PC games are often stripped-down versions
after: Your Android phone runs Steam games locally - no streaming, no extra hardware
Games use your phone's GPU directly, so they work offline
An open-source project you can inspect - no hidden services or accounts beyond Steam
uses_note: DroidDeck is 29 days old. Press coverage shows gameplay on handhelds, but detailed benchmarks are from individual uncontrolled tests - not formal reviews.

coverage.title: DroidDeck 0.3.0 brings Steam Deck-style controls and frame generation to Android
Free app lets Android phones play Steam games without a PC
This new Android app makes your gaming handheld feel more like a Steam Deck

steps: Check your device: you need Android 9 or later with a Qualcomm Adreno 650 or newer GPU (most flagship phones from 2021 onward, or handhelds like the AYN Odin 3 or Retroid Pocket 5). About 4 GB of free space for the runtime.
[Download DroidDeck v0.6.0](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/releases) - install the APK (allow installs from unknown sources if prompted).
Launch DroidDeck, sign into [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/), and pick a lighter game first (2D or older 3D titles work best). The app will download the runtime on first launch.

footprint.disk: About 3 GB for the runtime, plus 1.1 GB for optional desktop components. Games need their full install size on top (typically 5 to 50 GB per game).
footprint.runs_on: Android 9 or later with a Qualcomm Adreno 650 or newer GPU. v0.6.0 also supports Meta Quest 2/3/3S (VR headsets) and several XR glasses (VITURE Pro, RayNeo, Rokid). Mali, Xclipse, PowerVR, and Adreno 710 GPUs are not supported.

best_for: Gamers who want their Steam library on an Android phone without streaming
Owners of Android gaming handhelds looking for a Steam Deck alternative
Tinkerers who enjoy testing game compatibility on new hardware
skip_if: Your phone has a non-Qualcomm GPU (Mali, PowerVR) - not supported yet
You want a plug-and-play experience - this is early software and many games need tweaking
You're happy with cloud gaming (GeForce Now, Xbox Cloud) and have good Wi-Fi

alternatives.name: Winlator

watch: **Beware fake download sites.** The project warns about impersonation sites using its name and logo. Download only from the [official GitHub releases page](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/releases).
**29 days old, beta software.** Game compatibility is limited and performance varies by device. Notebookcheck characterizes it as beta with limited hardware validation.
**GPU requirements are strict.** Qualcomm Adreno 650 or newer only. Mali, PowerVR, Xclipse, and Adreno 710 GPUs are not supported - that rules out most Samsung Exynos and Google Tensor phones.
**One Reddit user bricked their controller mapping** after updating to v0.3.0 (fixed by switching to X360 mode). Expect rough edges between updates.
